'''Giuseppe Di Giovanni, [[Cavaliere]]''' (born 24 May 1968; Palermo, Italy) is a Professor of [[Human Physiology]] and [[Neuroscience]] at the [[Magna Græcia University]] of Catanzaro, Italy.
  
== Early life ==
Di Giovanni Giuseppe received his PhD in [[Neuroscience]] from the [[University of Chieti]], [[Italy]] and was a [https://www.um.edu.mt/profile/giuseppedigiovanni postdoctoral fellow] at [[Yale University]], CT, USA.

== Career ==
He served as a Senior Lecturer of Human Physiology at the Faculty of Medicine and Surgery, [[University of Palermo]]. Later he became Professor of [[Human Physiology]] and [[Neuroscience]] at the [[University of Malta]], as well as an [[Honorary Professor]] at the Neuroscience Division of the School Biosciences at [[Cardiff University]], UK.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/people/view/1144052-di-giovanni-giuseppe|title=Professor Giuseppe Di Giovanni - People - Cardiff University|work=Cardiff University|access-date=2018-11-01|language=en}}</ref> He is also an [[Adjunct Professor]] at [[Korea University]], School of Medicine in Korea, Seoul. He is currently a Full Professor of Human Physiology at the Medical School of the [[Magna Græcia University]], Catanzaro, Italy. His main research interests are in experimental neurology and [[biological psychiatry]]. Specifically, he is interested in the pathophysiological role of [[cannabinoids]] and [[serotonin]], and especially of the 5-HT<sub>2C</sub> receptors, in brain disorders, such as [[epilepsy]], depression, drugs of abuse and [[Parkinson's disease]]. He has published more than 160 [https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=DLEmKqgAAAAJ&hl=en articles] in top biomedical journals including Nature Medicine and Nature Neuroscience, 15 books and several journal special issues.

He is the Past-President of the "[https://www.medneuroscisociety.org/ Mediterranean Neuroscience Society (MNS)] the President of the Malta Physiological Society and the Treasurer of the Malta Neuroscience Network. He is the Editor-in-Chief of the prestigious [[Journal of Neuroscience Methods]] by Elsevier, Amsterdam, Netherlands and the Editor of the book series "[http://www.springer.com/series/7668 The Receptors]" by Springer, USA and serves as associate editor for the CNS Neuroscience & Therapeutics by Wiley.
On 28 May 2020 he was awarded the honour of [https://www.quirinale.it/onorificenze/insigniti/362165 Cavaliere] (Knight) of the [[Order of the Star of Italy]] by the [[President of the Italian Republic]] [[Sergio Mattarella]].
He was listed among the World’s Top 2% Scientists ranking for his work in 2019<ref>Baas, Jeroen; Boyack, Kevin; Ioannidis, John P.A. (2020), "Data for "Updated science-wide author databases of standardized citation indicators"", Mendeley Data, V2, doi: 10.17632/btchxktzyw.2</ref> and 2020<ref>Baas, Jeroen; Boyack, Kevin; Ioannidis, John P.A. (2021), "August 2021 data-update for "Updated science-wide author databases of standardized citation indicators"", Mendeley Data, V3, doi: 10.17632/btchxktzyw.3</ref> in the field of Neuroscience. In 2022, he was elected a member of [[Academia Europaea]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Giuseppe Di Giovanni|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Di_Giovanni_Giuseppe|work=Member|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2024-09-13}}</ref>  due to his achievements in [[Physiology]] and [[Neuroscience]] research and  [https://ibro.org/meet-the-elected-ibro-officers-and-regional-committee-members Secretary-General] of [[IBRO]], the International Brain Research Organization, for the term January 2023 – December 2025.
